A Q3 trading update on a 15-analyst FTSE 100 name with guidance expected to be reiterated: PRT YTD (£5.7bn at end-July plus £1.7bn UBS) looks set to print under the £11bn-by-October 2025 comparator and M&G's halved Q3 asset-management flows read across weakly, into a stock at multi-year highs that has sold three of its last four results-type releases.

The release carries the FIRST FY27 outlook — a scheduled guidance event on a 2-analyst name — against an uncut Edison FY27 PBT of £78.2m (+12%), while INSEE's October French household confidence fell 5 points to 80, the lowest since June 2013, in the final month of FY26 and in the market the company itself blamed for its 26.7% June warning; partly offset by a low FY26 H2 bar (£36.3-41.3m needed) and a stock already down 15.7% over 20 sessions, which is why abs_move is large and p_up only modestly below 50.

Flows are the only unseen line and the line this stock trades on; two separate reads point flat-to-positive — Ashmore's $1.1bn of Q1 inflows with 15-year-low redemptions in the same quarter, and N91's own AUM falling 1.4% against a market mix down roughly 2% — into a stock with a flat 20-day run-up and 0.2% short, tempered by post-period EM weakness and a name that has sold earnings growth twice.

The period was pre-released on 5 Oct, so the open lines are NAV and per-share FFO: GBP:EUR moving 1.1516 to 1.1701 reverses the FX translation hit that drove last H1's -0.9% NAV and the -2.88% reaction, and Landsec's UK surplus to 30 Sep supports valuers, but cost of debt 2.5%->3.5% and ~6% more shares leave per-share FFO flat beside an 11.3% rent roll, so the set nets to near zero on a low-volatility name.
